chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal, from Thalabah ibn Maymun, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the prayer behind the Mu'tilah (those who differ, i.e., Sunnis), and he said, 'They are with me no more than the walls.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on praying behind Sunni Muslims according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) uses the metaphor of 'walls' (al-judur) to describe the Mu'tilah (Sunnis), indicating that while their prayers may be valid, they lack the spiritual depth and distinctiveness of the Shia prayer, serving merely as a physical barrier or backdrop rather than a shared spiritual entity. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential view of *ikhtilaf* (difference) in ritual practice, where the Imam distinguishes between the mechanical validity of the prayer and its qualitative essence. The metaphor suggests that praying behind them is permissible but not ideal, as they do not fully embody the specific Shia understanding of worship.
